_provenance.experiment: Refresh of the SICM-on-variational-inference per-step ablation that produced the Design-section 5.11x and 3.51x numbers.
_provenance.cause: FIX 1 (per-site whole-slice DynamicUpdateSlice in impulse::constrainPosition / impulse::unconstrainPosition) changes gp_pois_regr's per-step cost, which selects two sites (alpha, HalfNormal, positive support; f_tilde, Normal, real support) and therefore reassembles 9 position elements through the transform path. scale_family_mvn selects a single site (tau) and takes the pre-existing single-slice bypass in both functions ('if (slices.size() == 1) result1D = slices[0];'), so it is structurally unaffected by FIX 1 and serves as the control.
_provenance.driver: Reactant.jl/test/probprog/svi_sicm_benchmark.jl, unchanged. Same methodology as the 2026-07-05 evidence: n = 8, 300 SVI steps, AutoNormal guide, Adam learning rate 0.01, 1 particle, init_scale 0.1; per-step cost is the best of 8 timed repetitions divided by 300; SICM is toggled with Reactant.Compiler.DEBUG_PROBPROG_DISABLE_SICM (DEBUG_PROBPROG_DISABLE_OPT is held false in both settings, so this isolates SICM and is not the flat-versus-region ablation).
_provenance.environment: julia --project=test -t 32, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty, JULIA_NUM_THREADS / OPENBLAS / MKL / OMP = 32, XLA_FLAGS=--xla_cpu_multi_thread_eigen=true, matching run_pplbench.sh --device cpu --threads 32. Reactant.jl/test/LocalPreferences.toml points at the same libReactantExtra.so as the benchmark tree (md5 88ec2c261e1d5069b0dfa91ce6c7d505).
_provenance.replication: The driver was run 3 times end to end; per-step values and ratios are reported per run with the median.
_provenance.caveat: The 2026-07-05 reference numbers were produced on a different build of the compiler stack. scale_family_mvn is the control: it is provably untouched by FIX 1, so any movement in its ratio is attributable to other compiler changes between 2026-07-05 and this build, not to FIX 1.

hlo_structural_check.purpose: Direct confirmation that FIX 1 is live in the loaded binary. The 2026-07-05 gp_pois_regr HLO carries one dynamic_slice and one dynamic_update_slice per position ELEMENT from the old per-element reassembly (9 elements: alpha 1 + f_tilde 8). Under FIX 1 the reassembly emits one dynamic_update_slice per SITE (2) and no dynamic_slice.

verdict: The HLO structural check confirms FIX 1 is live in the loaded binary and confirms the intended split between the two models: gp_pois_regr's emitted HLO loses all 9 per-element dynamic_slice operations (one per position element: alpha 1 plus f_tilde 8) and drops from 11 to 4 dynamic_update_slice operations, while scale_family_mvn's counts are unchanged at 2 dynamic_update_slice and 0 dynamic_slice because its single selected site takes the bypass. Despite that op-count reduction, gp_pois_regr's SICM on-versus-off ratio barely moves against the 2026-07-05 reference, whereas scale_family_mvn's ratio, which FIX 1 cannot touch, moves a great deal. The control moving more than the treatment means the ratio change recorded here is not attributable to FIX 1: at n = 8 the position reassembly is simply not a measurable share of the per-step cost of the variational loop. The movement in scale_family_mvn's ratio comes from other compiler changes between 2026-07-05 and this build, concentrated in the SICM-off setting.
